positions.sector: Energy — 2x leveraged crude oil futures ETF
positions.catalyst: THE 60-DAY US-IRAN DEADLINE EXPIRED YESTERDAY WITH NO DEAL, AND THE ESCALATION IS RUNNING INSIDE THIS HOLDING WINDOW. The accord Trump signed at Versailles in June set a 60-day clock to end the war and reach a nuclear agreement; that clock ran out Monday August 17 with the two sides FURTHER APART than when it started. Trump has publicly refused to extend the truce, threatened to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of the US, and restored the naval blockade of Iran after cancelling the waivers that had let Iran sell oil internationally. Fighting has flared anew in Lebanon. There has been no sign of compromise on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and no sign detailed nuclear talks have even begun. THE PHYSICAL SUPPLY DATA IS THE HARD PART OF THIS, NOT THE RHETORIC: after attacks on tankers, Hormuz transits collapsed to FIVE commodity vessels on Saturday and ZERO on Sunday, against 31 during the prior weekend. Roughly a fifth of global seaborne oil normally moves through that channel and it is currently running at a small fraction of pre-war volume. EIA's August Short-Term Energy Outlook already flags a large drawdown in global inventories from the continued Hormuz disruption and expects prices to stay elevated until flows normalise and stocks are replenished. Brent ended Monday above $90 and trades around $88.5; WTI is ~$85 and rose again this morning. CRUCIALLY, OIL IS THE ONLY THING BID IN A RISK-OFF TAPE: US futures are lower, Polymarket puts just a 27% chance of a higher S&P open, bond yields are rising, and semiconductors are being liquidated (SMH -3.06%, MU -4.9%, SNDK -5.8%, SK hynix -5.2%, NVDA -2.1%). A crude position is the one long here whose driver is orthogonal to the equity unwind.
positions.driver: LONG UCO — ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil, 2x WTI futures, 100% of capital, at 43.76. WHY CRUDE AND WHY 2x: this is a hard-dated event that CROSSED ITS DEADLINE inside the last 24 hours, which is the mandate's definition of a strong fresh catalyst, so 2x is the leverage that fits — not 1x, which under-pays a genuine supply shock, and not 3x, which I rejected on the grounds below. The payoff is the reason to own it: a Hormuz closure or a US strike is the classic fat right tail where crude gaps 10-20% in hours, while the realistic left tail is a de-escalation headline that gives back the war premium — and much of that premium is ALREADY in at Brent ~$88.5, so the downside is a partial round-trip rather than a collapse to fundamentals. Asymmetric. WHY 2x CRUDE AND NOT 2x ENERGY EQUITIES: GUSH (2x E&P) at 42.61 and ERX (2x energy sector) at 104.05 are the same theme but carry equity beta into a tape that is actively selling risk — on a day the Nasdaq is being liquidated, energy equities get half the commodity move and all of the market drawdown. ERX's pre-market book was also unusable, 104.97 bid against a 114.65 ask. Crude futures isolate the catalyst. EXECUTION INTEGRITY MATTERED IN THIS PICK AND IS WORTH RECORDING: the dashboard feed is serving prior-session closes for equities during pre-market — it showed SOXL at 151.53 while Robinhood's live pre-market print was 135.34, a 10.7% gap. UCO is the rare name where the canonical feed and the live book AGREE: proxy 43.76 against a Robinhood bid/ask of 43.77/43.90 and a 10:27Z pre-market print of 44.15. The entry of record is real, not a stale mark. CHOSEN OVER: (1) SOXS 3x inverse semis — directionally the right read on the loudest move in the market, and the honest reason I passed is that it is already up roughly 9-10% pre-market on the chip liquidation; buying it now is textbook chasing under the mandate's own ban, and I would be entering a 3x fund after the move rather than before it. (2) SOXL 3x long semis at a 135.34 pre-market print, -10.7% — a falling knife with no catalyst to catch it; ADI reports tomorrow, NVDA is two weeks out. (3) OILU 3x crude — right direction, more leverage, rejected on two counts: the pre-market book was 45.81 bid / 56.98 ask, a spread wide enough to destroy the trade on entry alone, and 3x on crude that is already carrying a war premium at $88.5 Brent gives back too much on any de-escalation headline. 2x is the leverage the risk supports. (4) USO 130.29 / BNO 51.97 — the unleveraged expressions; correct thesis, but 1x on a moonshot book forfeits the payoff the event deserves when a liquid 2x is available at a tight spread. (5) SQQQ 3x inverse Nasdaq at 37.74, already +3.6% pre-market — index leverage that is both a chase and a diffuse expression of what is really a chip-specific unwind. (6) BITX 2x Bitcoin at 12.11 — BTC is 64,126 and range-bound with no dated catalyst; paying 2x for chop. (7) NUGT 2x gold miners at 167.80 — the other geopolitical hedge, but silver is +37% over five weeks to a record and miners just ran their hottest five days since 2008; 2x into a parabola is the worst downside protection on the board, and the actual catalysts (Fed minutes tomorrow, Jackson Hole later) are outside the window. (8) HOLDING SOL-USD a fourth day — the Agave v4.2 activation we were positioned for EXECUTED yesterday. The catalyst is spent, the trade closed +$18.24, and holding into the post-event drift is how a won thesis turns into a lost one. (9) 100% CASH — defensible on a risk-off day, but it forfeits the only live, escalating, hard-dated event on the board. Entry 43.76 = canonical dashboard live feed, asOf 2026-08-18T10:42:36Z, cross-checked against Robinhood real-time. Stop 40.26 (-8%, the 2x band).
positions.risks: A DE-ESCALATION HEADLINE IS THE DOMINANT RISK AND IT IS BINARY, INSTANT, AND OUTSIDE MY CONTROL. The same president who refused to extend the truce yesterday can announce a resumption of talks, a Hormuz reopening, or a new Versailles round at any hour; oil would give back 5-8% immediately and 2x doubles that. This is the specific way the trade loses, and it loses fast. THE WAR PREMIUM IS ALREADY PARTLY PAID: Brent at ~$88.5 against EIA's $85 Q3 forecast means the market has already priced meaningful disruption, so the marginal surprise from more of the same is smaller than the headlines suggest — the trade needs genuine ESCALATION, not continuation, to pay. DEMAND DESTRUCTION IS A LIVE SECOND CHANNEL: if today's equity unwind broadens into a growth scare, crude can fall WITH stocks despite the supply story, which would mean being long the one asset I picked for its orthogonality and getting the correlation anyway. STRUCTURAL DRAG ON THE INSTRUMENT: UCO is a 2x DAILY-RESET fund holding WTI futures, so it suffers both volatility decay on a chop-and-reverse path and roll drag if the curve is in contango — over a single 24h hold the decay is small, but it is a persistent negative and it means UCO will underperform 2x the spot move on any non-trending day. EVENT CALENDAR SITS JUST OUTSIDE THE WINDOW: EIA weekly inventories print Wednesday and Fed minutes land the same day — both are capable of moving crude hard, and both land AFTER our rotation, so we carry the risk of positioning into them without capturing them. OPEC+ RESPONSE is a further overhang; spare capacity being released, or any signal of it, caps the upside. MITIGANTS: leverage stepped down deliberately from the available 3x to 2x, which is the largest single piece of downside protection here; a hard -8% stop at 40.26; an entry that is NOT a chase — crude is up only ~0.6% today, nowhere near the 8-10% extension ban, unlike SOXS and SQQQ which I rejected precisely for that reason; an instrument whose canonical and live prices agree to within a penny, so there is no stale-mark risk in the fill; deep liquidity in the front WTI contract; and a driver that is genuinely uncorrelated to the semiconductor liquidation dragging the rest of the tape down.
